statement.p: A lobster tank in a restaurant is 1.5 m long by 0.75 m wide by 80 cm deep. Taking the density of water to be 1000 \mbox{kg/m}^3, find the water forces
on the bottom of the tank: Force =
on each of the larger sides of the tank: Force =
on each of the smaller sides of the tank: Force =
(include for each, and use g = 9.8 \hbox{ m/s}^2)

static.solution:
g=9.8 meters/sec{}^2:
Bottom: \hbox{Force } = 1000(0.8)(1.5)(0.75)(9.8) = 8820 \hbox{ N}. On the larger sides, \hbox{Force} = (1000)(1.5)(9.8)\int_0^{0.8} (0.8 - x) \ dx = 4704 \hbox{ N}. And on the smaller sides, \hbox{Force } = (1000)(0.75)(9.8)\int_0^{0.8} (0.8 - x) \ dx = 2352 \hbox{ N}.
